stem: A client using a combined oral contraceptive has missed one hormonally active pill by 24 to less than 48 hours. What should the nurse advise?

options.A: Take the missed pill as soon as possible and continue the remaining pills at the usual time.
options.B: Discard the missed pill and take only the next scheduled pill.
options.C: Discard the current pack and begin a completely new pack immediately.
options.D: Take two additional pills at the next scheduled time regardless of when the missed pill is remembered.

rationale: CDC U.S. Selected Practice Recommendations state that if one hormonally active combined oral contraceptive pill has been missed for 24 to less than 48 hours, the client should take the missed pill as soon as possible and continue the remaining pills at the usual time, even if this means taking two pills on the same day. A is correct.

source_original.stem: A client taking a combined oral contraceptive asks the nurse what to do after missing one pill, mentioning a friend told her to just double up on the very next scheduled pill instead of taking the missed one separately. The nurse should generally advise the client to instead:

options.A: Take the missed active pill as soon as possible and continue the remaining pills on schedule
options.B: Discard the missed pill and take only the next scheduled pill at the usual daily time
options.C: Discard the current package and begin a completely new package immediately after one miss
options.D: Take two additional pills at the next scheduled time regardless of how late the pill is

source_original.rationale: General guidance for a single missed combined oral contraceptive pill is to take the missed pill as soon as remembered (which may mean taking two pills in one day) and continue the rest of the pack as scheduled, though clients should always be directed to the specific product's labeling or consult their provider/pharmacist, since instructions can vary and backup contraception may be recommended depending on the number of missed pills and timing in the cycle.
source_original.source_detail: Late/missed combined oral contraceptive: take one late/missed active pill as soon as possible and continue remaining pills, even if two pills are taken the same day; 2024 U.S. SPR; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Specified the exact CDC interval for one missed active pill (24 to <48 hours), removed the friend-based cue, and aligned the answer directly with U.S. SPR 2024.

audit_findings.claim_audit: The one-pill 24 to <48 hour recommendation is directly stated by CDC.

distractor_audit.C: Not indicated for one missed pill.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: The exact missed-pill interval makes A unique.
